As the new school year begins, more and more Americans are expressing support for an outright ban on student cellphone use in classrooms.

As the new school year gets underway, the chorus of voices supporting bans on iPhone use in classrooms continues to grow.

Yes, it's still July, but somehow summer has ended early. My kids head back to school today and tomorrow — marking the second year in a row that the first day of school falls outside of August.

Apple is getting in on the seasonal action with its annual Back to School promotion, offering eligible students and educators a gift card of up to $150 when they purchase select Mac and iPad models through August 27. Shoppers in multiple states can also take advantage of limited-time sales tax holidays.

While back-to-school discounts are a welcome perk, smartphone use during class time is increasingly falling out of favor.

The most upvoted comment comes from GreenPizza.

I haven't seen any data to support the idea that 'students having phones reduces the risk of school shootings.' In fact, reducing distractions in the classroom would let us get back to the actual point of going to school — learning.

A new survey from Pew Research Center found that 77% of U.S. adults support banning middle school students from using phones in classrooms. That figure is up from 68% in 2024 and 74% in 2025, with just 18% now opposed to classroom bans.

Support for stricter bell-to-bell bans is growing even faster. For the first time, the share of Americans who support banning student phone use throughout the school day now outweighs those who oppose it.

The report also notes that younger generations remain less enthusiastic about classroom bans and bell-to-bell bans, though support has risen across all age groups since 2024. The full report can be read here.

What do you think? Should schools restrict iPhone use to class periods, implement a full bell-to-bell ban, or leave it up to students and parents? Let us know in the comments.
